response.query: What sample size and power-calculation methods are recommended for EEG HMM studies to detect time-resolved emotional state differences in continuous-report paradigms?
response.answer: For EEG HMM studies, a sample size of 30-50 participants is typically recommended, and power calculations should use G*Power or simulation-based methods to ensure adequate statistical power.

results.title: EmoTrans attention based emotion recognition using EEG ...
results.content: The model integrates features extracted from EEG signals in the time, frequency, and wavelet domains as well as facial video data to provide a comprehensive understanding of emotional states. * Multimodal Emotion Recognition: In contrast to earlier studies that used only EEG data, the current study integrates varied EEG features from different domains i.e., time, frequency, and wavelet with facial video data, thereby greatly improving the robustness of classification. This is an approach that has combined the feature of the frequency domain with asymmetry analysis, while catching the minute differences in brain activities of different emotional states quite effectively, hence improving the overall accuracy of our human behavior recognition model. In the frequency domain evaluation, EmoTrans has outperformed all other models in all the emotion categories; it had a maximum accuracy value of Arousal (85.69%), Valence (87.69%), Dominance (89.62%), and Liking (87.62%) as shown in Fig. 25 This, therefore, confirms its superiority to classify emotions with EEG signals using the frequency domain.
